algorithm: Structural template speculative drafting with XML tag prediction
summary: Drafts from an observed structural template (SUMMARY/CAPTION/REASONING/CONCLUSION XML tags) that forms the first 36 tokens of every output. After the answer letter, drafts the closing tag. Uses online adaptation to track per-stage acceptance rates.
key_insight_from_real_data:
All 24 observed real outputs share an identical 36-token structural prefix: '<SUMMARY> <THINKING_OF_SUMMARY> </SUMMARY>

<CAPTION> <THINKING_OF_CAPTION> </CAPTION>

<REASONING> <THINKING_OF_REASONING> </REASONING>

<CONCLUSION> '. 23/24 outputs are simple MC answers (A/B/C/D) plus closing tag. 1/24 has longer conclusion text.

1_structural_template.description: Drafts known XML structural prefix from current position
1_structural_template.coverage: ~86% of total tokens for simple MC answers

2_conclusion_closing.description: After answer letter appears in decoded_text, drafts closing tag ' </CONCLUSION>'
2_conclusion_closing.observed_acceptance: 5/5 tokens when no period in answer; retries in 1 step if period present

3_bigram_fallback.description: Last-resort 1-token bigram prediction for unexpected output regions

return_format: Returns {'text': str} so trusted tokenizer handles encoding. Returns [] when no confident draft available (requests one ordinary AR step).

budget_handling.truncation_method: character budget estimated at ~5 chars/token; trusted tokenizer enforces real limit

online_adaptation.mechanism: Infers acceptance from generated_token_ids length delta (accepted = delta - 1)
online_adaptation.reset_detection: 5 signals: first_call, empty_generated, question_changed, position_backward, decoded_shorter
online_adaptation.current_usage: Tracks stats; future versions will adjust strategy ordering based on observed acceptance

real_dev_results.v071_result: 13.4% WORSE than baseline - wrong structural assumptions (natural language templates vs actual XML tags)

position_template_controller.held_out_speedup: 8.08x (12 train / 12 test split, includes 1 complex outlier)
position_template_controller.generalization_ratio: 65.6% (driven by 1 complex output in test set; structural prefix generalizes 100%)

suffix_match_controller.note: Conservative controller; underperforms because char-per-token approximation is imprecise in simulation

realistic_speedup_estimate.note: Verification overhead factor accounts for draft verification costing more than 1 AR step. Even at 2x overhead, v0.8.0 is 6x better than v0.7.1.

assumptions: The XML structural template (36 tokens) generalizes to all questions, not just 24 dev outputs
Most questions have simple MC answers (letter only); complex conclusions are rare
Returning text with trusted tokenizer produces same token IDs as direct token ID return
Standard speculative decoding semantics: accepted prefix + 1 target token per draft call
Verification of K tokens costs ~1.2-2.0x an autoregressive step (not Kx)
expected_failure_modes: Complex/open-ended questions with long conclusions (~4% of dev set): structural prefix still helps but conclusion area is unpredictable
Period after answer letter ('B.'): causes 1 extra AR step before closing tag kicks in
Questions with non-standard output format (not observed in 24 dev outputs)
Tokenizer edge cases where character-level position tracking is imprecise
Guard replay outputs: 0 observed in 24 dev outputs, but could change structural pattern

next_discriminating_gpu_experiment.hypothesis: Structural template drafting (v0.8.0) achieves >5x speedup over baseline on dev seeds
next_discriminating_gpu_experiment.null_hypothesis: Speedup < 2x (verification overhead eats most gains, or template doesn't generalize)
ablation_plan: A1: Full v0.8.0 policy (structural template + closing + fallbacks)
A2: Template only (no conclusion closing) - measures closing tag contribution
A3: Conservative suffix-match controller - measures algorithmic difference
next_discriminating_gpu_experiment.primary_metric: Mean latency ratio across 5 dev seeds
next_discriminating_gpu_experiment.decision_rule: If ratio > 0.7 -> investigate verification overhead; if ratio < 0.2 -> approach validated, optimize further

diagnostic_checks_passed: contract_checks: 22/25 pass (3 failures are old test assumptions about natural-language format)
edge_cases: OK (None values, missing keys, whitespace, near-end)
contract_checks_note: 3 'failures' are from check_contract.py tests written for v0.7.1 natural-language assumptions. v0.8.0 correctly uses XML template format. All type-safety, budget, and edge-case checks pass.

cpu_testbed_results.v071_synthetic_word_level: 1.43x (synthetic test data, now known to be wrong format)
cpu_testbed_results.note: v0.7.1 word-level results were based on wrong structural assumptions about output format

incumbent_verified.result: incumbent is WORSE than baseline; v0.8.0 should easily beat it

uncertainties: Exact verification overhead factor (1.2x vs 2.0x) - only GPU measurement can tell
Template generality beyond 24 dev outputs - held-out validation supports 100% structural prefix generalization
Complex conclusion frequency - 1/24 in dev, may differ on full set
Period-vs-no-period ratio in answer letters - 2/23 simple answers had periods (8.7%)

robustness.output_agreement: 100% (speculative decoding only accepts verified tokens; quality gates pass on v0.7.1)
robustness.bounded_resources: O(1) in history length; fixed template strings; observer uses bounded deques
robustness.graceful_degradation: Falls back to [] when template doesn't match; same as baseline

v0_8_0_changes.change_summary: Complete architectural change from natural-language template matching to XML structural template drafting. Based on actual observed output structure from 24 real development outputs.
added: Two genuinely different controller implementations (position-based and suffix-match)
v0_8_0_changes.expected_improvement: 6-9x better than v0.7.1 (from 1.134 ratio to ~0.14-0.19 ratio)
v0_8_0_changes.basis: Token-level offline replay on 24 real observed outputs
